newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - Alusaf to boost Gencor first half.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Alusaf to boost Gencor first half.

text.p: Gencor Ltd is due to report increased earnings for the six months to end-December next week on the back of strong contributions from its aluminium and coal interests, analysts said.

Gencor is due to report its half year results on February 25 and analysts expected a healthy showing from the South African mining house with diversified interests in gold, platinum, base metals and coal.
Analysts polled by Reuters predicted the company would report earnings per share of 64.1 cents against the 48.5 cents in the six months to end-December 1995. The range was 60-69 cents.
An interim dividend of around nine cents, with a range of 9-10, could be declared against the seven cents previously, they said.
The analysts singled out Gencor subsidiary Alusaf Ltd as the biggest contributor to the expected increased earnings. Gencor bought complete control of aluminium producer Alusaf last year.
"What will be nice to see is the first impact of a 100 percent owned Alusaf which should be the biggest driver of these earnings," said Barnard, Jacobs and Mellet analyst Robynn Kearney.

Alusaf's Hillside smelter -- commissioned in June last year with a design capacity of 460,000 tonnes of aluminium per year -- is operating above design capacity and the company reported year net income of 165 million rand last August up from 57 million rand in the same period in 1995.
"The big kicker has to be Alusaf...it was not even to full production a year ago. Now it is in fact over full production," Kearney added.
Kearney and other analysts said Gencor earnings may also be boosted by its Ingwe Coal Corporation Ltd which reported sharply increased half-year earnings on February 13.
"Ingwe and Alusaf, (but) especially Alusaf, are going to contribute tremendously," Standard Equities analyst Manny Rahan said.
Rahan said the impact of lower world aluminium price would to a large extent be offset by the sharp drop in the rand against the dollar.

Analysts expected Gencor earnings to be affected by lower profits from ferro-alloy producer Samancor Ltd, mainly due to higher costs at the troubled Columbus Steel joint-venture with the state's Industrial Development Corporation and Highveld Steel and Vanadium Ltd.
They predicted income from its offshore arm Billiton International and overseas assets would also contribute significantly to Gencor results.
"I look for some very good results from the offshore assets, they still had the benefits of the weaker rand in the first six months of their financial years," Kearney said.
"The real key is what Billiton is going to do in dollars," said one analyst who asked not to be named.

Analysts said Gencor remained their top choice in the sector and said recent developments, including the company raising its stake in Colombian nickel mine Cerro Matoso on Tuesday to 98.88 percent, were very positive.
"All of it is very positive, management is very aggressive, focused on low cost deposits and Gencor is certainly one of my picks in the sector," said another analyst.
